intended_object: The condition on a commutative ring R and a size n that the determinant-one diagonal torus of SL_n(R) separates coordinates: for every pair of distinct indices i ≠ j there is a diagonal matrix diag(t_1,…,t_n) with unit entries and ∏ t_r = 1 such that t_i ≠ t_j. Equivalently, every root character t ↦ t_i t_j⁻¹ is nontrivial on the torus. Inferred from the docstring and from how the library uses it as a hypothesis for normalizer and Weyl group results.
explanation:
The body says exactly what the docstring says. For all distinct i, j in Fin n there is a family t : Fin n → Rˣ with ∏ (t r : R) = 1 and t i ≠ t j. A unit family with product 1 is the same thing as a diagonal element of SL_n(R). Comparing t i and t j in Rˣ is equivalent to comparing them in R, because the coercion from units is injective.

The degenerate cases behave as expected. For n ≤ 1 the condition holds vacuously, which fits, since then there is no pair of coordinates to separate. Over 𝔽₂ or 𝔽₃ with n = 2 it fails, which is also correct: the only diagonal elements of determinant one there are ±I, so the two coordinates are never separated. The library proves the expected sufficient condition (a unit a with a² ≠ 1) and the expected consequence (Rˣ is nontrivial when n ≥ 2).

On generality: the condition is stated for any commutative ring, which is the natural setting. Indexing by Fin n matches the library's own definitions of the diagonal torus and of SL_{n+1} built on Fin n, so it is not a meaningful restriction. Mathlib has no predicate of this kind.
